title: PQC Assessment Map Room
purpose: Frame a six-step stakeholder conversation about what the assessment maps, which evidence creates the map, how evidence becomes report content, what the public reference implementation can demonstrate, and which leadership actions unblock the next step.

syntheticBoundary.label: Synthetic reference demonstration
syntheticBoundary.statement: All estate records, measurements, dates, actions, and outcomes shown in this briefing are synthetic examples. The demonstration contains no customer data, has no live enterprise connections, and does not represent enterprise progress or completeness.

briefingSteps.name: Mission
briefingSteps.headline: Build an evidence-backed map before drawing risk conclusions
briefingSteps.primaryMessage: Phase 1 identifies the cryptographic estate, its dependencies, the supporting evidence, and the remaining limitations. Phase 2 uses the accepted map to analyze technical exposure and business impact.

briefingSteps.name: Estate
briefingSteps.headline: The map spans ten connected parts of an enterprise
briefingSteps.primaryMessage: The domains identify where cryptography may exist or be governed. They orient the conversation without implying that every possible source, asset, or dependency has already been found.

briefingSteps.name: Method
briefingSteps.headline: Authoritative source facts become traceable assets, dependencies, and reports
briefingSteps.primaryMessage: Surveying means identifying suitable source systems, establishing an approved read-only route, recording provenance-bearing observations, correlating them into canonical assets and dependencies, and preserving findings and limitations through reporting.

briefingSteps.name: Position
briefingSteps.headline: Implementation state and estate state are different measures
briefingSteps.primaryMessage: Verified public-reference artifacts can demonstrate the method, but they do not establish customer access, enterprise evidence, report readiness, or production capability. The two states remain separately labeled and are never combined into one progress percentage.

briefingSteps.name: Demonstration
briefingSteps.headline: A narrow synthetic flow shows how several sources assemble one connected map
briefingSteps.primaryMessage: Five initial source contract packs produce synthetic observations, assets, relationships, dashboard measurements, and an explicit limitation. The example proves presentation and contract behavior only within its declared two-region scope.

briefingSteps.name: Action
briefingSteps.headline: Leadership moves the map forward by assigning routes, owners, and dates
briefingSteps.primaryMessage: The briefing closes by naming the responsible role, requested outcome, required date, and delivery consequence for each unresolved enabling action. The presentation does not record approval or mutate project systems.

initialSourceTracks.scopeStatement: This is an initial source track and does not represent the complete enterprise estate.

initialSourceTracks.name: PKI and certificate lifecycle
initialSourceTracks.purpose: Provide certificate, issuing authority, lifecycle, status, trust, and association facts without collecting private-key material.

mapFlow.title: Evidence-backed assessment map flow
mapFlow.scopeStatement: This flow explains how suitable enterprise source facts can become reviewable assessment evidence and report content. It does not imply that a source has been approved, connected, or shown to cover an enterprise.

nodes.name: Enterprise source
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: A platform, repository, service, inventory, or approved export that may contain source-native facts relevant to the assessment.

nodes.name: Approved access and source profile
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: The operating function, scope, interface, authorization route, fields, identifiers, constraints, and fallback needed before collection begins.

nodes.name: Evidence observation
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: A dated fact with source provenance, collection context, and evidence status; it is not yet a broad claim about the estate.

nodes.name: Canonical asset
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: A normalized representation of a cryptographic object, deployment, application, repository, software component, data store, device, or other in-scope item.

nodes.name: Dependency and business context
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: Evidence-backed relationships connecting assets to certificates, software, services, owners, data, regions, vendors, environments, and critical processes.

nodes.name: Finding or evidence limitation
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: A supported condition requiring attention or an explicit statement describing what the available evidence cannot establish.

nodes.name: Phase 1 current-state assessment report
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: The reviewable account of scope, method, observed estate, dependencies, findings, evidence quality, and disclosed limitations.

nodes.name: Phase 2 risk and business-impact analysis
nodes.plainLanguageMeaning: Analysis that uses the accepted Phase 1 baseline to evaluate exposure, consequences, migration constraints, prioritization, and unresolved decisions.

stateSeparation.rule: Verified public-reference implementation state and synthetic estate state must remain in separately labeled panels and must not be represented as one progress measure.

actualReferenceImplementation.label: Verified public-reference implementation state
actualReferenceImplementation.scopeStatement: This state reports only the existence and validation status of artifacts in the public reference repository. It does not report customer access, customer evidence, enterprise coverage, report acceptance, or production readiness.

statusFacts.statement: Five independently authored synthetic source contract packs are available for deterministic component and presentation proof.
A checked-in synthetic Phase 1 fixture demonstrates source-to-observation-to-asset-to-dependency processing within a narrow two-region scenario.
A rebuildable synthetic dashboard projection carries explicit scope, denominator, freshness, confidence, limitation, and projection-lag semantics.

syntheticDemonstration.label: Synthetic estate demonstration state
syntheticDemonstration.scopeStatement: The selected evidence-arriving state illustrates a narrow two-region scenario. Its measurements and relationships cannot be used to describe a customer estate, enterprise coverage, report acceptance, or production state.

demonstration.title: Two-region synthetic Phase 1 evidence flow
demonstration.explanation: The demonstration uses five initial source contract packs to show how source records can become observations, eight canonical assets, eight evidence-backed dependencies, a bounded dashboard projection, and one visible evidence limitation.

lineageExample.explanation: Synthetic application, TLS, certificate, repository, and software-analysis observations are connected to show how one service context can be assembled while retaining a visible ownership limitation.

leadershipRoles.name: Enterprise coordination lead
leadershipRoles.purpose: Route each source track to the smallest responsible function and ensure that a named next action and date are returned.

leadershipRoles.name: Enterprise platform enablement lead
leadershipRoles.purpose: Coordinate the approved non-production runtime, data, identity, security, tooling, and access paths needed for implementation.

leadershipRoles.name: Project governance lead
leadershipRoles.purpose: Confirm project-system administration, assessment authority, escalation, decision ownership, and acceptance routing.

leadershipActions.title: Route the five initial source tracks
leadershipActions.context: Implementation can begin only after each starting track is associated with a responsible function, candidate source, approved access route, and dated next action.
leadershipActions.requestedOutcome: Assign a responsible function and next-action owner for every initial source track, with a route for resolving an unavailable or unsuitable source.
leadershipActions.consequenceIfUnresolved: Source profiling and access work cannot proceed, so the affected areas remain an unmeasurable evidence limitation and report readiness cannot advance.

leadershipActions.title: Confirm the technical enablement route
leadershipActions.context: The assessment implementation needs approved paths for the application runtime, relational data service, identity, secrets, telemetry, repositories, and read-only source access.
leadershipActions.requestedOutcome: Name the enabling functions, required requests, responsible owners, and target dates for the non-production technical foundation.
leadershipActions.consequenceIfUnresolved: The reference implementation can continue with contracts and synthetic tests, but no enterprise deployment, live capability claim, or source integration can be made.

leadershipActions.title: Confirm project execution and authority paths
leadershipActions.context: Backlog administration, decision routing, escalation, evidence review, and the Phase 1 read-only boundary require clear operating ownership.
leadershipActions.requestedOutcome: Confirm the project-system administration path, read-only assessment authority, escalation route, decision owners, and acceptance functions.
leadershipActions.consequenceIfUnresolved: Work may continue only as local preparation; execution state, approvals, and gate readiness cannot be represented as established.
